clue.text: Stop outside right line for one on 26

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for stop goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to stop is to cease

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt beyond some right-hand line, aimed at someone taking part in industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is the second half of the 19/26 answer; in cricket a batsman 'on strike' is the one facing the bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the batsman facing the bowler stands at a white marked line on the pitch, the popping one.

clue.text: Old woman with bad asthma revered wise men

parts.note: one's old woman is one's mother, informally ma

indicators.note: bad says the letters of asthma are in a poor, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A mother with a bad chest goes to holy sages, presumably for a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title of respect for a great-souled sage, as given to Gandhi.

clue.text: George Armstrong, 19, more astute when tackling Spurs winger

indicators.note: tackling as in taking hold of: the word for more astute grips the extra letter

parts.note: cuter means sharper, more astute

indicators.note: a winger plays on the edge, so this takes the edge letter of Spurs

explanation.surface: A football report: a player named George Armstrong being cleverer when tackling a Tottenham Hotspur winger.
explanation.walkthrough: George Armstrong was also a real Arsenal winger, so the football surface hides the American cavalry commander of Little Bighorn. Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was the US cavalry officer killed at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.

definitions.meaning: a member of the standing army rather than a reservist
the 19 across word as an adjective, usual or normal, as in the common run of things

explanation.surface: A soldier wearing his kit, serving in the army under a commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a professional army man, the adjective even or steady, and the adjective normal or common.

clue.text: No end of bile Puck produced in 19

indicators.note: produced suggests the remaining letters are made into something new, a rearrangement
each of the two words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The setter, Puck, spewed endless bile in a general sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it trims the last letter from both bile and Puck, leaving BIL and PUC to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, 19 across and this word overlap: open to or shared by everyone, as in the general public.

clue.text: Trade union in a state, for real

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for the union inside the letters for the state

parts.note: Cal is a short form of California

explanation.surface: A trade union in a real state of affairs, or operating in an American state for real.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean existing in fact rather than in theory or imagination: genuine.

indicators.note: running wild says the letters are out of control and scattered

parts.note: 3 down is the Little Bighorn commander, George Armstrong

explanation.surface: Animals running loose in the time of an American frontier commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures are living beings, especially animals as opposed to people.

definitions.meaning: a horse, the Suffolk breed of heavy draught horse
a blow with the fist, a hit

explanation.surface: Someone getting on to land a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk Punch is a British breed of heavy horse; 26 is a hit or blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Suffolk breed of horse that can be ridden and a blow from the fist.

parts.note: Mac in Scottish surnames means son of
Arthur is the legendary king of Camelot

explanation.surface: A Scottish king's son described as a military leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas MacArthur led US forces in the Pacific in the Second World War and in Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas MacArthur was a five-star American army commander, so he is an example of the 19 across rank.

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase, from the first

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone us often and walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To clout someone is to hit them hard, as 26 can mean.

indicators.note: the right-hand half of the letters, and only that half, is turned back to front

parts.note: the two cross-references read separately: 19 gives Ney, Napoleon's marshal, and 26 as a verb meaning hit gives RAM

explanation.surface: A footballer in 1926 playing at right half-back, an old position.
explanation.walkthrough: Right half-back looks like a football position, but it turns only the right half: NEY RAM becomes NEY MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Neymar is the Brazilian forward who played for Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain.

clue.text: A king has one coal supply in 19

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: supply is read as supplely, flexibly: the letters of coal bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch holds a store of fuel as part of a general stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as the adverb supplely (pliantly), not the noun, signalling the rearrangement of COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was the Roman commander who conquered much of Britain, father-in-law of Tacitus.

definitions.meaning: the union call for every worker to walk off the job during the 1926 stoppage

explanation.surface: A complete rallying call heard during the 1926 national stoppage.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1926 the TUC called millions of British workers to stop work together for nine days in support of the miners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means total or complete, and was also the cry calling every worker out on strike.

parts.note: intimate friends are close
by means times, as in two by four

explanation.surface: Intimate moments that are near at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean near or nearby, within easy reach.

clue.text: Oddly, only the Guardian's after first instalment of Camberwick Green?

indicators.note: after puts the letters that follow behind the opening letter
the opening part of the word, its first letter
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of only

parts.note: the paper speaks of itself as we, so its possessive is our

explanation.surface: A newspaper claiming only it shows the first episode of a children's programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberwick Green was a 1960s British children's stop-motion TV series. The question mark marks green as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is one example of a hue, so the question mark signals a definition by example.

parts.note: the word bride with its bottom letter wiped off leaves four letters, which read as B, short for one word of the title, and RID, a synonym of the other

explanation.surface: A film about a bride cleaning up after a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is treated as wordplay. B is short for born (as in genealogies) and RID means free, so together they give BRID, which is 'bride' losing its bottom letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Born Free is the 1966 film about Joy and George Adamson raising Elsa the lioness.

clue.text: A Green Line outing's a hit, leading to more than one day out for many?

definitions.text: more than one day out for many?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go first, leading to the word for hit
an outing sends the letters out of their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A Green Line coach trip proves a success, the first of several days out for a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Line is a London coach company, so the surface suggests a day trip. The 1926 stoppage lasted nine days, so many had more than a day off work.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1926 nationwide walkout by British workers lasted nine days: a long stretch away from work for millions.

clue.text: Guess Puck's into a car with extra storage space

indicators.note: into puts the setter's contraction inside the car word

parts.words: a car with extra storage space
parts.note: an estate car has a large load area behind the seats
Puck is the setter, so Puck's means I'm

explanation.surface: A guess that the setter fits into a roomy car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge roughly, to make a guess at a figure or value.

definitions.meaning: the 19 across word as an adjective, widespread or liked by many
the Ford ..., a British family car of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A military commander driving an old Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Popular was a cheap British-built Ford sold from 1953 to 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: Common among people at large, as in popular opinion, and the name of a cheap British Ford model.

clue.text: Harlot cycling around with X, a seductive character

indicators.note: cycling around moves letters from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: X is the Roman ten, written in figures as 10, which looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A prostitute riding a bike with a partner, a seductive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking HAR from the front of HARLOT to the back gives LOTHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a libertine in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, now names any womanising seducer.

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters as a bottle holds liquid

explanation.surface: A boast that the house perfume smells lovely, sold by the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are smells, pleasant or otherwise.

clue.text: Far from enjoying a night out

indicators.note: out means the letters are out of place, disordered

explanation.surface: Someone at a party who would rather be at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is the opposite of liking it, so detesting is far from enjoying.

clue.text: Creative person, twice briefly in 19 practice

definitions.meaning: a painter or sculptor, a maker of works
the short form RA, Royal Academician, sits inside the 19 across word and inside practice, so it appears twice

explanation.surface: A creative type who practises, but only briefly and rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a stock abbreviation for a painter. It appears in the middle of the 19 across word and near the start of 'practice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter or other maker of art is the standard example of a creative person.

parts.note: Att is an abbreviation for attorney
Robert E Lee was the commander of the Confederate army

explanation.surface: A former prime minister and the attorney general together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attorney 19' reads as the Attorney General, a government law officer, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951.

parts.note: to boot is to kick
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Giving a senior officer a hard kick.
explanation.walkthrough: William Booth founded the Salvation Army, whose leader holds the rank of General.
explanation.definitionFit: William Booth was the first leader of the Salvation Army, which gave him the military title.

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is as heard when spoken

parts.note: 3 down is the Little Bighorn commander, George Armstrong
Mary is the Virgin, mother of Jesus

explanation.surface: An American commander chatting with the Virgin Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the surname in 3 down plus MARY sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, usual and common are near synonyms of what is done by custom.

parts.note: to mouth off is to rant

explanation.surface: It is fine to shout one's mouth off, in a general way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S Grant led the Union armies in the American Civil War and later became president.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S Grant was the Union army commander in the American Civil War, so an example.

clue.text: Adult locked up in Wakefield, missing green area once part of Yorkshire?

indicators.note: in puts the adult and locked-up letters inside what is left of the town
missing means the word for green is taken away from the town name

parts.note: a green is a grassy field
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
pent means shut in, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A grown-up imprisoned in Wakefield, a Yorkshire city, with no open space.
explanation.walkthrough: Wakefield is a West Yorkshire city with a well-known prison, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A wapentake was an old administrative subdivision of Yorkshire and other northern and eastern English counties.
